cases.title: Cases
cases.body: Every test case in this project — authored, not derived from a run. A case is an ordered list of Action + Expected steps with a state, a priority and an owner, identified as TC-001 onwards. Cases are the unit everything else here refers to: plans group them, runs execute them, and coverage counts them. Drafting with AI writes real cases here, linked back to the acceptance criterion each one verifies.

plans.title: Plans
plans.body: Named subsets of the cases, for when "run everything" is the wrong answer — a smoke set, a release checklist, a regression pass. A plan references cases rather than copying them, so editing a case updates every plan holding it. Adding a case to a plan does not change the case.

features.title: Coverage
features.body: Coverage seen from the work rather than from the suite: each feature and bug, how many cases claim to test it, and how many of its acceptance criteria any case actually names. "Uncovered" means no case links to it — which is the gap worth acting on, because an untested feature looks identical to a passing one until something breaks. The count on this tab is the number of uncovered work items, not the total.

runs.title: Runs
runs.body: What has actually been executed, from two sources in one history: runs Fabric drove itself against one of your environments, and runs your CI reported. Each row carries its source mark, who triggered it, and its result. Failures become findings for a person to triage — Fabric never files a bug on its own.

questions.title: Questions
questions.body: Open questions raised while drafting or reviewing cases — an ambiguity in a criterion, a flow with no stated expected result. They live here rather than as comments on a case so that the thing blocking coverage is visible without opening every case to find it.

reviews.title: Pull requests
reviews.body: Pull requests Fabric has read from your connected repository, each stored with the exact diff it fetched. Right now that is all this does: it reads and shows, so you can see what a review would be based on before any review exists. Reading a pull request uses the repository credential this project is already connected with, and is recorded in the audit log.

about.label: About Atlas
about.title: Your codebase, mapped
about.intro: Atlas turns a connected repository into a living map of your system — every module, capability, and the relationships between them — so you and your agents can reason about the whole codebase, not just one file at a time.
about.analyseBody: Atlas scans your connected repository at a specific commit and extracts files, modules, imports, and dependencies.
about.mapBody: It groups everything into business capabilities and technical modules, then computes the relationship graph between them.
about.exploreBody: Read the Overview for a high-level summary, or open the Graph to trace how any capability or module connects to the rest.
about.askBody: The Atlas Assistant answers questions grounded in the graph — what depends on what, and what a change would ripple into.
about.editBody: Draw your own connections, set each one's type and description, delete or restore them, or re-map with AI — Atlas saves your edits and the assistant reasons with them.
about.systemBody: Connect more repositories and Atlas wires them into one cross-repo map — the calls, shared libraries, and shared domains between your services — so the assistant reasons across the whole system.
about.footerNote: Atlas flags **re-analyse recommended** when the branch has drifted from the last analysed commit — re-run it to keep the map current.

projectDescription.name: Project description
projectDescription.description: Describe the project in more than a sentence — what it is, who it is for, what it has to do.
projectDescription.tooltip: Fabric reads this before anything else: it is the seed for generated documents, roadmap suggestions and recommendations. Under 50 characters there is not enough here to work from. This item disappears once a PRD exists, which supersedes it.

featureSnapshot.name: Feature Snapshot
featureSnapshot.description: Define the major capabilities or feature areas Fabric should understand.
featureSnapshot.tooltip: Feature context helps Fabric generate better documents, roadmap items, and recommendations. For early projects, this can be lightweight and refined over time.”

techStack.name: Tech Stack
techStack.description: Tech stack context helps Fabric tailor architecture, API, QA, and engineering handoff outputs. For Discovery / Planning projects, this can be preliminary.
techStack.tooltip: Visit the overview page to define your project's tech stack.

contextSource.name: At least one context source added
contextSource.description: Add at least one meaningful context source.
contextSource.tooltip: Fabric needs project context to produce useful documents, recommendations, and AI answers. Context can include uploaded files, pasted notes, transcripts, links, connected tools, or repositories.

additionalContextSources.name: Additional context sources added
additionalContextSources.tooltip: Additional sources improve Fabric’s ability to cross-check assumptions, identify gaps, and generate higher-quality outputs.

chatAppConnected.name: Chat app connected
chatAppConnected.description: Connect a relevant Slack or Teams workspace/channel.
chatAppConnected.tooltip: Chat context helps Fabric capture decisions, urgency, requirements, and follow-up work discussed outside formal documents.

meetingTranscripts.name: Meeting transcripts available
meetingTranscripts.description: Add or connect relevant meeting transcripts.
meetingTranscripts.tooltip: Meeting transcripts help Fabric recover decisions, rationale, open questions, and requirements that may not exist in formal documents.

pmSystemConnected.name: PM system connected
pmSystemConnected.description: Connect the project’s work management system.
pmSystemConnected.tooltip: PM-system context helps Fabric import existing work, reduce duplicate planning, and align Roadmap with execution.

codebaseConnected.name: Codebase connected
codebaseConnected.description: Connect a readable codebase when development has started.
codebaseConnected.tooltip: Codebase access helps Fabric ground technical documents, validate requirements against implementation, and support engineering handoff.

wikiConnected.name: Wiki Connected
wikiConnected.tooltip: Wiki context can improve long-lived documents and reduce missing background information.

knowledgeBase.name: Knowledge Base
knowledgeBase.description: Connect a relevant project knowledge base.
knowledgeBase.tooltip: Knowledge base context can improve long-lived documents and reduce missing background information.

businessCase.name: Business Case Document
businessCase.description: Create a Business Case when the project needs value or investment framing.
businessCase.tooltip: A Business Case helps Fabric understand why the project matters, what value it should deliver, and how success may be evaluated.

proposal.name: Proposal Document
proposal.description: Create a Proposal when scope or commitments need to be captured.
proposal.tooltip: A Proposal helps Fabric understand agreed scope, delivery expectations, assumptions, and commitments that should shape downstream work.

prd.name: Product Requirement Document (PRD)
prd.description: Create a PRD to anchor product scope, goals, and requirements.
prd.tooltip: A PRD gives Fabric a strong source of truth for users, scope, requirements, expected behavior, and acceptance criteria.

architecture.name: Architecture document
architecture.description: Create or add an Architecture document for the product’s technical structure.
architecture.tooltip: Architecture context helps Fabric understand system components, dependencies, integrations, and technical constraints.

apiSpec.name: API specification exists
apiSpec.description: API spec exists when API behavior is in scope.
apiSpec.tooltip: API specs help engineering and QA understand contracts, integrations, and edge cases.

technicalSpec.name: Technical Specification
technicalSpec.description: Create a Technical Specification when implementation details need to be defined.
technicalSpec.tooltip: A Technical Specification helps engineers understand the implementation approach, technical constraints, and system behavior needed to build the product.

qaStrategy.name: QA Strategy exists
qaStrategy.description: QA strategy or testing plan exists.
qaStrategy.tooltip: QA planning improves release confidence and clarifies quality gates before delivery.

roadmapPopulated.name: Roadmap Populated
roadmapPopulated.description: Add or import Roadmap work items.
roadmapPopulated.tooltip: Roadmap items help Fabric understand planned work and connect requirements, recommendations, and execution.

pmSyncEnabled.name: PM-system sync enabled
pmSyncEnabled.description: Sync work items to your project management system.
pmSyncEnabled.tooltip: Sync keeps Fabric and your connected project management system aligned so work can be managed in both places when configured.”

terminalStatuses.name: Terminal statuses defined
terminalStatuses.description: Map completed or closed PM-system statuses.
terminalStatuses.tooltip: Terminal statuses help Fabric recognize completed, canceled, or removed work and keep Roadmap clean.

teamMembers.name: Add Team Members
teamMembers.description: Add project team members to Fabric.
teamMembers.tooltip: Fabric’s value increases when the team can share context, review outputs, and collaborate in the same project workspace.

workCaptureTranscripts.name: Work capture from transcripts enabled
workCaptureTranscripts.description: Fabric can capture work items discussed on discovery and team meetings.
workCaptureTranscripts.tooltip: Fabric can propose new or updated work items from meeting transcripts when transcript capture is configured.

workCaptureChat.name: Work capture from Chat
workCaptureChat.tooltip: Fabric can propose new or updated work items from monitored chat channels when chat capture is configured.

releaseNotes.name: Release notes configured
releaseNotes.description: Fabric can generate and distribute release notes.
releaseNotes.tooltip: Fabric can help generate release notes so stakeholders stay informed about delivered work.

atlasExplored.name: Codebase explored in Atlas
atlasExplored.description: Fabric can help you understand your codebase.
atlasExplored.tooltip: Atlas helps users understand code structure, dependencies, and implementation details after a codebase is connected.

securityScan.name: Security scan completed
securityScan.description: Fabric can help you understand vulnerabilities in your codebase.
securityScan.tooltip: Security scanning helps identify vulnerabilities or risks in the connected codebase.
